heading: Gradual circuit formation, then removal of memorizing components, can underlie grokking
definition: the generalizing circuit (e.g. a Fourier algorithm for modular addition) forms gradually and memorizing components are removed later, so continuous progress measures anticipate the jump.
summary: Several independent groups find internal progress before grokking, but gradual circuit formation followed by removal of memorizing components remains disputed as a general explanation. Some circuits or probe measurements change only during generalization, and larger-model studies support only parts of this explanation.

suggested_status.by_scale: Toy/small models (algorithmic, synthetic two-hop reasoning and Ising phase-classification tasks): C for the unqualified chronology, alongside R2-level evidence for conditional hidden progress. <1B: partial mechanism/probe evidence; full conjunction unresolved. 1-10B: partial patching/routing evidence; full conjunction unresolved. No V2 coverage recorded at 10-100B or >100B.
suggested_status.reason: The unqualified gradual-circuit chronology has explicit challenges: binary-increment causal alignment changes with generalization (10.24963/kr.2026/95#r38–r41), parity-match feature energy remains near zero through the plateau (arXiv:2608.25813#r4, #r6, #r7), and strong-decay Fourier assembly is described as abrupt (arXiv:2606.32000#r42). The checks also relabelled V2.against[7], [9] and [16] as challenges, each for one condition. (1) Ising-CNN energy and magnetization correlations stay roughly constant across layers during the plateau. The authors describe weight-decay-dominated dynamics with no apparent hidden model formation (arXiv:2502.01739#R3). (2) Under second-hop full augmentation, a parameter-sharing knowledge-graph Transformer groks without forming the intended bridge-recovery circuit; the alternative mechanism is unidentified (arXiv:2601.09049#R6, #R7). (3) On complex-number multiplication over F7, an MLP algebra-alignment probe (Arep) stays low before grokking and rises sharply during it. This comes from a figure-only row, and alternative measures are untested (arXiv:2602.19533#R9). The other findings in those items stay limits_scope: the LMN and refit findings in against[9], the mean-field MLP in against[7] and the EMNIST findings in against[16]. Pack headers class arXiv:2502.01739 and arXiv:2602.19533 as reviewed and arXiv:2601.09049 as other (ACL Annual Meeting). By author matching, none of the challenge studies above shares authors with an original. arXiv:2502.01739 and arXiv:2601.09049 also support V2 in other conditions. In the first, mean Fourier IPR improves through the modular-addition MLP plateau (arXiv:2502.01739#R2). In the second, the natural-grokking regime recovers the bridge before final-answer accuracy stabilises (arXiv:2601.09049#R3). Conditional hidden progress also has functional evidence, including circuit probing and DAS (arXiv:2311.04354#r3, #r6). counts, built before the checks and not reflecting this relabelling: versions.V2.verdicts.challenges.studies = 3 and versions.V2.verdicts.limits_scope.studies = 55. Until the counts are rebuilt, the challenge-labelled studies are 10.24963/kr.2026/95, arXiv:2608.25813, arXiv:2606.32000, arXiv:2502.01739, arXiv:2601.09049 and arXiv:2602.19533 (the last three each for one condition only). versions.V2.studies_by_size and versions.V2.coverage_by_operation show small-model and 1-10B coverage but no larger-size entries. These records support a contested broad formulation rather than absence of hidden progress.
suggested_status.open_questions: Which tasks and regularizers yield gradual identified-circuit formation rather than abrupt acquisition? Can identified memorization removal be separated causally from readout alignment or continued consolidation? Do the Ising-CNN, second-hop-augmentation and Arep-probe challenges hold under other continuous progress measures in the same conditions, or only for the quantity each study measured? A matched-recipe replication with continuous circuit/component tracking and prospective timing and success prediction, including failed runs and realistic pretraining, would clarify the status and scale limits.

source.title: Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability
source.authors: Neel Nanda; Lawrence Chan; Tom Lieberum; J. Smith; Jacob Steinhardt

original_result.setup: The study tracked loss using only selected Fourier frequencies, sparsity (concentration at fewer Fourier frequencies), and squared weights in a one-layer transformer learning addition modulo 113.
original_result.result: Loss restricted to key Fourier frequencies fell before test loss, which dropped suddenly after circuit formation as memorizing components were removed. In this later phase, Fourier sparsity increased sharply and the decline in squared weights sped up.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: The V2 mechanism at model sizes 10–100B and above 100B.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V2.studies_by_size contains <1B, 1-10B and not stated, with no 10-100B or >100B entry; versions.V2.coverage_by_operation likewise has no entries at those sizes. Available large-model examples concern OLMoE 7B and LLaMA-3.1-8B/Qwen2.5-7B.

untested.what: A quantitative forecast validated across operations and architectures using the complete identified circuit-and-memorization decomposition.
untested.basis: The packs' untested-parts lines distinguish circuit analysis without a quantitative timing forecast from entropy/ILDR prediction without identified memorization removal. Checkpoint extraction also lacks continuous trajectories. Relevant evidence: arXiv:2302.03025#r6, arXiv:2604.13123#R7, arXiv:2604.20923#r1 and arXiv:2603.23784#R31. counts: versions.V2.main_rows_by_operation and versions.V2.coverage_by_operation list measurement, probing, removal and interventions separately; they do not establish the combined forecast.

untested.what: Prospective discrimination of successful and failed runs using early latent-circuit extraction or self-patching signals.
untested.basis: No prospective predictor evaluation is reported in the chaining study. Appendix D restoration percentages are conditioned on eventual generalization (arXiv:2607.08393#D01 and arXiv:2607.08393#D02); failed runs also exhibit off-diagonal restoration (arXiv:2607.08393#D04). arXiv:2603.23784#R28 establishes final extractability in a non-generalizing model, without testing continuous development, anticipation or memorization removal. counts: versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.probing and versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.measurement establish coverage of these operations, without documenting prospective success discrimination.

untested.what: An identified generalizing circuit, measured later removal of identified memorizing components, and advance timing prediction during realistic language-model pretraining.
untested.basis: Untested-parts lines for routing, copying and grammatical pretraining leave this combined mechanism unresolved. Routing correlations begin after the accuracy rise; copying induction scores have no established jump-timing relation; grammatical probes do not identify removed components. Relevant rows: arXiv:2506.21551#r9, arXiv:2409.09281#r8, arXiv:2606.00230#r29 and #r41. counts: versions.V2.studies_by_stage and versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.measurement.by_stage include base coverage, so pretraining itself is tested; the gap is the joint mechanism.

untested.what: Direct identification and temporal tracking of the memorizing components removed in coset-group networks, deep arithmetic Transformers, digit-arithmetic encoder–decoders and modular division.
untested.basis: The respective untested-parts lines leave memorization removal unresolved. Available measurements concern coset structure, head suppression, representation/readout dependence and spectral utility: arXiv:2312.06581#r3, arXiv:2603.29262#R8, arXiv:2604.13082#R5 and arXiv:2609.17571#r17. counts: versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.removal shows removal experiments exist globally, without establishing that the removed components in these settings are memorizing components.

wording_issues.issue: Circuit-specific alignment (n=16, α=0.5) and Task 1 parity-match rule-feature energy can remain weak through the plateau and change mainly at the transition. In the P=97 MLP with strong weight decay (0.1), Fourier assembly is explicitly described as abrupt.
Fine-tuned models retain heuristic heads while effective size increases. GNN simplification removes components of an earlier sufficient generalizing circuit, without a behavioral jump.

wording_issues.phrase: continuous progress measures anticipate the jump
wording_issues.issue: This holds for selected measures and conditions. Fourier-density timing changes with threshold; under ILDR's fixed step-3000 baseline, detection occurs at step 3500 after the held-out threshold at step 3000 for training fraction 0.4, and coincides with the held-out threshold at step 3100 for training fraction 0.5. Update-eigengap detection can occur after generalization or fail on ReLU; embedding-rank compression can continue substantially afterward.

Leading internal signals do not establish the full causal chain or an eventual jump. Early patch-restorable representations occur in failed per-fact chaining runs in experiments involving LLaMA-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B. Task-aligned filtering can supply answer structure to a lookup memorizer. Second-hop full augmentation produces behavioral grokking without formation of the intended bridge-recovery circuit, challenging the proposed mechanism in that regime.

Much evidence concerns Fourier concentration, kernel alignment, compression or decodability without complete circuit identification. The planted-core theory assumes the useful feature rather than discovering it.

method_sensitivity.factor: Probe method, layer and internal quantity
method_sensitivity.what: Circuit probing and DAS indicate gradually causal a² development, while conventional probes also decode irrelevant b². LMN reveals hidden progress at the first hidden layer but plateaus at other measured layers. Within the eNTK report, Fourier-feature alignment is continuous while the second spectral cliff coincides with grokking. Within the QNN run, output Fourier structure precedes improvement while the sharp stability drop accompanies it.

method_sensitivity.factor: Task-aligned projection, reading basis and frequency restriction
method_sensitivity.what: Full-family Fourier filtering produces generalization in a constructed lookup memorizer; early high filtered accuracy therefore cannot determine whether a generalizing circuit has been learned. Synchronization timing depends on reading basis and single-crossing versus held rules. Weak cross-seed timing correlations alone do not test V2's claim of progress before the jump. A Transformer ridge readout leads only under frequency restriction; its ordinary all-frequency version trails the network.

method_sensitivity.factor: Spectral matrix, rolling window, activation and loss
method_sensitivity.what: Weight-matrix and parameter-update spectra can place changes on opposite sides of grokking. Update-eigengap signatures differ between x² and ReLU, and rolling-window choice changes control false positives. Output-preserving narrowing occurs in the reported Transformer but not the MSE mean-field MLP; architecture and loss differ together.

The radial-suppression study contrasts progressive Fourier formation under an activation-norm penalty with abrupt assembly under strong weight decay. Its high coherence-threshold timing is internally inconsistent and does not establish failure of subthreshold anticipation. Other modular-addition MLP reports show slowly rising Fourier IPR or phase alignment during memorization, under different recipes and measurements. Low-rank decay imposes abrupt early Query/Key stable-rank collapse, but this measure cannot determine generalizing-circuit formation or memorizing-component removal and supplies no V2 exception. These comparisons do not establish a matched-recipe contradiction.

With a fixed step-3000 baseline, ILDR at training fraction 0.4 occurs at step 3500 after the held-out threshold at 3000; at training fraction 0.5 both occur at 3100. V2 detector anticipation is respectively reversed and absent; these results do not establish absent behavioral generalization. In the addition-modulo-97 Transformer baseline, entropy precedence concerns the first evaluation with an entropy decrease >0.05 over a five-evaluation rolling window, rather than an interchangeable point-threshold crossing. The GMM indicator crosses early in non-grokking controls.

method_sensitivity.factor: Representation availability, downstream readout and supervision
method_sensitivity.what: Freezing embeddings suppresses structure and grokking in the embedding study. In ExPLAIND's single-layer MOD-113 Transformer, pipeline transplants or outer-layer changes expose generalization; the final phase aligns outer layers around an established pipeline under high relative regularization influence. Identified memorization removal remains untested. In the six-layer base-8 encoder–decoder, residues are decodable early; encoder transplants and decoder rewinds shorten the plateau, localizing a readout bottleneck without identifying the full circuit-development or memorization-removal sequence (cannot_determine for V2). Readout belongs to the complete circuit. Natural-grokking composition supervision produces early bridge recovery, while second-hop full augmentation produces behavioral grokking without the intended bridge-recovery circuit. The latter challenges that proposed mechanism; the alternative mechanism is unidentified.

In the rank audit's free-decay arms, frac-pre is 0.87 for the canonical LayerNorm-free Transformer, 0.66 for the MLP and 0.25 when LayerNorm is added. Lag conclusions also depend on compression tolerance. A separate LayerNorm-placement study finds configuration-dependent ordering of Fourier concentration, feature compressibility and grokking; its measurements differ from embedding rank.

method_sensitivity.factor: Thresholds, sampler settings and training phase
method_sensitivity.what: FFD at η = 0.5 approximately coincides with accuracy; lower thresholds can lag perfect accuracy, while higher thresholds converge too quickly. LLC estimates depend strongly on sampler localization and learning rate. Input sensitivity rises during circuit formation and falls during cleanup, while weight norm falls earlier but is flat during cleanup. Curvature-onset lead depends on learning rate, seed and sustained versus first-crossing grokking definitions.

method_sensitivity.factor: Ensemble, individual-run, neuron and layer aggregation
method_sensitivity.what: An ensemble effective-dimension precursor does not reliably characterize individual local-rule runs; neither result identifies gradual generalizing-circuit formation or memorizing-component removal. Gradual cleanup of one coset neuron does not establish whole-model anticipation. Digit-arithmetic head specialization varies across seeds, which alone does not qualify V2. OLMoE's final-layer routing edit distance increases after memorization, unlike the reported simplification elsewhere; this layerwise result cannot determine V2's circuit mechanism, which does not require every layer to simplify.

method_sensitivity.factor: Checkpoint, reconstruction, example order and circuit metric
method_sensitivity.what: Extracted-model performance depends on checkpoint, label noise and reconstruction, and can exceed the real network's performance even in failed runs. Final-checkpoint extractability cannot determine gradual circuit formation, forecasting or memorization removal. Example ordering changes learned frequencies and spectral trajectories; early Fourier structure does not establish absence of later memorization removal. The original baseline's restricted/excluded losses show pre-jump progress, while the public-checkpoint analysis places most explained-logit-variance growth after test-loss decline begins. Those metrics measure different quantities, and identical run identity is not established.

status_amendment.public_note: The assessment of this version now also weighs checked results that challenge it in an Ising-model classifier, a synthetic two-hop reasoning model trained with augmented data and a network learning algebra over a finite field: in each, the measured internal progress did not come before the jump, or the expected circuit did not form. The level is unchanged: the broad claim stays contested, while gradual hidden progress is still reported in other small-model settings.
